brief: For North Macedonia, indirect regulatory-timing signals concentrate in three publicly reachable layers: (1) hiring — MK-language job boards (vrabotuvanje.com.mk, kariera.mk), the NBRSM careers page and the aggregator bankarstvo.mk, which republishes bank compliance/AML/regulatory-reporting ads and preserves them after the originals expire; (2) training and events — ABIT (the dedicated MK banking academy), the Economic Chamber's finance seminars, MASIT/KIBS payment-standard workshops, the FIU's statutory AML officer trainings, IORRM's annual CPD programme, and commercial conferences (Finelevate, MicroBalkans, the EACHA annual conference hosted in Skopje); (3) awards and certifications — Global Finance-type bank awards and licence milestones, surfaced first through the MK business-press cluster (Faktor, Makfax, Biznisvesti, MKD, MIA), which functions mainly as a pointer layer to primary organiser sites. English-language search is effectively blind for this cell — no MK bank vacancy surfaced in English — so Macedonian-language querying is load-bearing, while Albanian remains an uncovered language and LinkedIn remains legally off-limits to automated collection. Principal weaknesses to close next: enumerating licensed non-bank PSPs/EMIs from the NBRSM register, resolving the canonical domains of the conferences named only in press coverage, and starting daily snapshots of job listings so a hiring-surge baseline can ever be computed.
